Enemy subs fight back with torpedoes, and all damage to the destroyer can be monitored and controlled, using pumps, flood controls and automated repair. If the attacker is successfully eliminated, the player's performance is evaluated and s/he may earn a promotion - and possibly a medal (for outstanding achievements). On the other hand, characters may be killed in action, or even demoted for desertion if a mission is aborted early.

The destroyers are modeled and named after real historical ships, and the game offers several features such as mission replay (letting you watch through the previous engagement with the enemy sub visible), a Sea Trials (practice) mode, and the Hall of Valor which records the history and statistics for every character created.

182360.overview:
Sint Nicolaas has been robbed! The thieves have taken his big sack full of presents and gingerbread cookies. In their run however, they weren't careful and presents started dropping out of the sack. Now Sint only has to collect the fallen cookies and presents and brind them to the right chimneys.

Sint Nicolaas is a platform game based on the the Dutch tradition of Sinterklaas. Jump across rooftops, pick up presents and cookies and watch out for birds and old fashioned TV antennas. The chimneys have a colored box and a number. You have to deliver the presents at the chimney with a matching color box and deliver as many cookies as indicated by the number. When you pick up presents they follow you in a string, similar to Flicky.

You can only deliver the present you first picked up. So if the present closest to you is red then you must first find a chimney with a red box. This gets tougher in later levels, where presents and matching chimney don't appear in order forcing you to backtrack parts of the level.

After each round there is a bonus game where you have to pick up 100 gingerbread cookies within a time limit, and there are platforms that disappear when you walk across them.

192368.overview:
The "HBO exclusive" movie, Soldier Boyz, was converted into this interactive, full motion video shooter for the PC which tests your hand-eye coordination, quick reflexes and memory of the events that transpire on-screen.

The story moves along by way of interactive video cut scenes in which you must decide whether to talk or shoot. The majority of them require a "shoot first and ask questions later" mentality. If you miss your target on the first try, you are able to replay the scene repeatedly until you are successful. If you guess wrong and shoot a "friendly", you are penalized by missing out on important information.

200511.overview: Expansion pack for the game Strike Commander. Adds 21 new missions and additional planes to fly.

202936.overview: Sky Cat is an action game with puzzle elements, where the player controls the space probe "Sky Cat" on the mission to find and rescue hostages on the alien enemy base. The probe breaks through the base, shooting the enemies with a laser in the way inspired by Thexder and solving the puzzles to overcome different obstacles toggling the electromagnet within its hull. Enemies are also shooting at the probe, trying to decrease its energy. The game is ended either with a successful mission accomplishment or with probe destruction.

204679.overview:
Golf's Best: St. Andrews - The Home of Golf is a golf simulation which allows you to experience the layout and character of one of the world's most famous courses, St. Andrews. Each hole is simulated exactly to scale. Undulations in the terrain, such as actual hills and valleys as found on the course as well as trees, bushes, water, sand and buildings are included. Wind also plays a part in the simulation. St. Andrews is a very windy course.

The game's display provides all the information required to make a great shot. Each hole provides an overhead and side view. Wind on the course is displayed by an arrow at the bottom of the screen which points in the direction in which the wind is blowing and that your ball will tend to blow. The larger the arrow, the harder the wind is blowing. It also shows you where the ball is, how far you are from the pin, what surface you are on and what stroke you are about to hit.

Order of play is determined by honors, the player with the lowest score on the preceding hole plays first. If you select hole 19, you will enter the clubhouse and your round will be over. Display the Scorecard by hitting the "4" key. Have a good round.

206711.overview:
This turn-based strategy game may be played against the computer or another human player (either in a hot-seat fashion or via modem). Each side starts out with a starbase, a bunch of ships, some cash, and one simple objective - total annihilation of the enemy.

Various ship types are available, from lowly scout to mighty destroyer, and each has its own stats: hull strength, energy, shields, scan range, the number of weapon bays, and moves per turn (firing a weapon counts as a move, too). The map grid is comprised of different sector types, some with associated astral phenomena that may help you, hinder you, or just throw you off course. Planets may be exploited for resources to bolster your treasury, and the starbase commissions new ships and performs hull repairs; additional fixes and upgrades (weaponry, shields and energy storage) can be found on trading planets - for the right price.

Two opponents playing over a modem connection can communicate using the text chat option. For single players who are feeling talkative, the game provides digitized voice feedback for pretty much any action... or lack thereof.

206845.overview:
Summer Number is an implementation of the game of MaxIt, realized in a retro style with anime-style drawings. The illustrations are hand-drawn using watercolors and markers.

A peculiarity of this game is that it is actually bootable and does not require any operating system to run. The system requirements are a 486 with 16mb of RAM, 800x600 resolution and a Soundblaster or compatible for audio. 

Because of the limited system requirements, it can run in the browser via an x86 emulator. It has also been tested with DOSBox-X and 86Box. Any computer from the late '90 with a PCI or AGP graphic adapter should be able to run it. Sound only works on Soundblaster and compatible cards though.

209064.overview:
SUPER-WUMPUS, by Jack Emmerichs, is an exciting computer game incorporating the original structure of the WUMPUS game described in the book "What To Do After You Hit Return," published by the People's Computer Company, along with added features which make the game even more fascinating.  Programmed in both 6800 assembly language and BASIC, the game is not only addictively fun, but also provides a splendid tutorial on setting up unusual data structures (the tunnel and cave system of SUPERWUMPUS form a dodecahedron).
 
The game begins with the player (hunter) somewhere deep within the Wumpus's cave, which consists of 20 rooms connected by tunnels. The rooms form the vertices of a dodecahedron and the tunnels form its edges. Therefore, each room has three tunnels connecting it to other rooms. The player starts in one of these rooms while the Wumpus is asleep in another. The hunter begins with five arrows or darts with which to shoot the Wumpus. Each arrow may be used only once. In the 6800 assembler version of the game, the object is to kill the Wumpus before he (she? it?) can find and eat the hunter. After watching several people become the blood-thirsty killers of an animal that they knew nothing about, and being of much more humane sentiments, I decided to change the object of the BASIC version of the game to that of immobilizing the beast so that it can be tagged with a beeper. When the beast wakes up, it will lead the hunter out of the caves and that is the only way the exit can be found. The play of the game is the same for both SUPERWUMPUS versions but there is less violence in the BASIC version.

217804.overview:
3D Space Fighter is a vertical-scrolling shoot 'em-up with high-resolution, pre-rendered graphics. According to the plot, at the start of the 21st century, mankind finally made contact with sentient alien life, but the aliens turned out to be hostile. Even though the extraterrestrial fleets had been detected from afar, Earth was not prepared and the first attack crippled the planet's defenses. Yet the humans unified their efforts and created a spaceship strong enough to stand against the enemy fleet, code-named Sigma Terminus. It is this ship that the player flies in the game, with the mission to remove the threat of alien invaders.

The gameplay consists of flying forward (vertically up) and shooting at advancing waves of enemy ships of different configurations that fly in various patterns. Occasionally, spheres that contain powerups appear on the screen, which after being destroyed drop their contents for the player to collect. These provide ammo for secondary weapons, shields, and other typical improvements. The player must watch out for other obstacles such as asteroids which may get in the path of the ship. The player's craft can withstand several hits from enemy shots and impacts, but the shields will not regenerate. Each level ends with a boss battle.

3D Space Fighter was marketed as shareware, with the unregistered version being time-limited to five minutes of play (per playing session). Registered users would receive a registration code to convert the shareware version into the full version without limitations.

217955.overview: Silly Knight is a game made for a recent game-making competition at the high-voltage.cz website. There is not a lot of plot; you're a knight and you have to get through a bunch of rooms of a castle / dungeon place. The game uses CGA 16-color (text) mode graphics, but still manages a charming look despite the low (effective) resolution. The controls are simple and responsive, and the game generally plays well, despite some cheap hits. For example, you go through a door, and are immediately hit by a skeleton. But since you have unlimited lives and there are continue beacons scattered around, it's not too much of a problem.

418177.overview: Silent Operation III: The Impossible Mission Under Water is a space-based horizontal shoot 'em up game that features a standard assortment of weapon power-ups. The game is known for its silent operation, which has been noted by some players as a notable aspect of the game. Despite its lack of sound, the game offers a unique shooting experience that captures the essence of the genre.

418181.overview:
Stormy World: The Three Kingdoms was developed by Soft-World International, a Taiwan-based developer, and published by the same company, sometimes in collaboration with Software Korea for distribution. The game is classified in the fighting/action genre and was designed to run on MS-DOS systems. Its storyline and characters are based on the historical events from the Three Kingdoms era of China, specifically drawing inspiration from works like Kim Yong's narratives.
The game was released in early 1995 worldwide and features standard DOS-era resolutions suitable for contemporary PCs of that period 
HFS DB. It is sometimes referred to by alternate names in different databases, but the core gameplay and title remain "Stormy World: The Three Kingdoms."

421024.overview:
This is the official game to the German SAT.1 TV Show "Bingo". To win the game you have to answer questions of several kinds: Nature, Sports, TV, Music, Geography etc.

You have a board with 25 squares (5x5 fields). Each question has a number between 1 and 25. For every correct answer you get a mark on your square field. To win the game you must get 5 marks in a row (horizontal, vertical or diagonal).

421048.overview: A German language quiz game. There is an English version however, that was never released, but a rom is available for that version. In this game, based on a TV quiz show, two pairs play against each other in several rounds and are expected to guess a five letter word per round in just five tries. They only get the first letter as a default and can only get closer to the solution by using the same letters as in the words they use as a solution.

421749.overview:
This game offers the possibility of having any of the teams of the Spanish Primera División (92/93 season) under your control, all that mixed in a top-down scrolled football simulator, which disposes of all the players, teams, stadiums, etc. with its real names and even voice effects for each one of the stopped-ball football situations.

You can play the typical friendly match, see a demonstration match or compete in the league (with option to save the game), but at the same time, you dispose of a huge database with information about all the teams and its players. That, along with a professional program of "quinielas" (football pools), which will allow you to win some money.

Years later (coinciding with the apparition of PC Fútbol 3.0), this game was informally considered by Dinamic as the first of the PC Fútbol series, it is, PC Fútbol 1.0.

424305.overview:
In an unique and interesting experiment, German department store giant Karstadt created a game that was advertisement and job recruitment in one box, and used its retail power to push it in the market at mid-price level.

Space Job is in essence a scifi life simulation; a 2350 adolescent strives for the fastest spaceship, the most beautiful girlfriend and the best career, but strictly within the confines of Karstadt's interplanetary empire. Starting as a trainee in one of four department store sections, you earn job reputation through stoic repetition of menial tasks - learning product prices by heart, sorting items in shelves, tidying up the storeroom in a Sokoban-style crate pushing subgame.

The quicker you do your daily chores, the more time remains for entertainment and private development - fitness training, gambling, movies, flirting, night school. An energy system balances your daily activities with periods of rest. Show endurance and personal progress, and promotion will unlock the full glory of department store management.

Despite its advertising character and indecent product placement, Space Job mediates commercialism with lots of tongue-in-cheek humor and light-hearted wordplay.

424926.overview:
Scythe is a 32-level megawad released by Erik Alm on April 8, 2003. The most distinguishing feature of Scythe is that most of its levels are smaller than average. Also, it was created in a matter of a few months, 31 levels by Alm, and Map 31 by Kim Bach (Torn). It is the most recent addition to the PWADs that Compet-n allows recording on. It was added to Doomworld's Top 100 WADs of All Time listing for the year 2003.

The sequel, Scythe 2, was released in June of 2005. A second sequel, Scythe X, had its first episodic release in September of 2009.

424959.overview: A Star Trek themed Doom mod

425001.overview: A Star Wars themed Doom mod.

425017.overview: STRAIN is a 32-level partial conversion for Doom II released in 1997 by the Alpha Dog Alliance. It features nine new or modified monsters through the use of DeHackEd, modified weapons, and a soundtrack written by David "Tolwyn" Shaw, Mark Klem, and Jon Landis.

425146.overview:
Suspended in Dusk (also known as SID) is a Doom II mod consisting of four levels, created by Esa Repo (Espi). It received one of the 2005 Cacowards. The player enters an infested UAC base and must fight his way to a small space ship to escape.

It was remarked for the careful attention accorded to texture use and alignment, and the intricacy of detailing achieved while remaining safely within the static limits of vanilla Doom.

Suspended in Dusk was originally released October 8, 2005.

425160.overview:
Scythe 2 is a 32-level megawad for Doom II created by Erik Alm and first released on June 6, 2005.[1] It was missing three levels that Alm eventually created for the re-release in 2009. The megawad is split into six episodes; upon finishing one, the player loses all his weapons and ammo and is forced to start the next episode with just a pistol. Each episode has a different setting and visual style.

The first Scythe was very popular, so this was a highly-anticipated sequel. It too was well-received, winning a Cacoward. While the original featured small, action-packed levels, Scythe 2 is filled with large, complex and detailed maps. This change has proven to be highly influential. In 2019, an article on the history of Doom mapping called Scythe 2 "the second most influential PWAD of all time after Alien Vendetta".

425223.overview:
SIGIL II is a sequel to SIGIL by John Romero and Romero Games.  It is a Doom episode, and was released December 10, 2023.

The digital OST was produced by Thorr. It also features an alternative and bespoke MIDI soundtrack by James Paddock (Jimmy), whose MIDIs were already featured in SIGIL.

425229.overview:
SIGIL (also styled SI6IL) is an episode WAD for Doom and Ultimate Doom that was released in limited editions on May 22, 2019, while the free release appeared on May 31, 2019. It was announced on Doom's 25th anniversary on December 10, 2018 by its designer, John Romero.

Although billed as a megawad with 18 maps, Romero clarified in an interview that each of the nine single-player levels includes a separate deathmatch arena, making it a standard episode. The levels were created using Doom Builder 2.

SIGIL was named as a runner-up at the 2019 Cacowards.

On December 11, 2019, Bethesda announced support for SIGIL as the first in a series of curated community WADs to be featured as an add-on for the Doom Classic Unity port, added alongside the official Final Doom and No Rest for the Living. The first version of the game allowing users to download SIGIL was released as an update on January 9, 2020.

A sequel, SIGIL II, was announced on August 15, 2021 and was released on Doom's 30th Anniversary, on December 10, 2023.

428518.overview: Build your kingdom with the help of hunters, soldiers, shipbuilders and more at your command. Develop elaborate settlements from a variety of over 25 different building types. Face the challenge of 49 different maps or use the easy-to-use map editor to create your own additional new worlds with dense forests, mighty volcanoes, vast mountains and more. Construct a fleet of ships, to explore uncharted waters and supply provisions to new islands.

428653.overview: Now you can design any city you can imagine and SimCity 2000 will bring it, and its resident Sims, to life. It has all the features, flexibility, art, animation, and power you need to create an environment of your dreams. Choose from a selection of bonus cities and scenarios to rule or ruin as you please. Build schools, libraries, hospitals, zoos, prisons, power plants, and much more... Lay down roads, railways, and highways. Explore the underground layer and build subways and utilities without compromising your aesthetics. Customize different buildings or design your own graphics sets from scratch.

428774.overview: Lo Wang. The very name strikes fear in fortune cookie-eating Mafia men and small children everywhere. He is the reason most ninja wannabees have sold off their combat sandals to the local pawn shop. Lo Wang is Shadow Warrior. #1 Assassin. #1 Yakuza abuser. #1 Freak fragger. #1 Mutant mutilator. #1 Reason to be scared of the dark. Enter the Land of the Rising Sun and spread ninja charisma like napalm for there are undead sumos to be uzied, samurai to be shurikened, and bulldozers to be boarded. Don’t forget to goose the geishas and make sure your dinghy isn’t hanging out...

428820.overview: The year is 2050. The ocean is the next frontier and war inevitably reaches the depths of the sea. As an independent mercenary working for a corporate conglomerate, you pilot the latest fighter subs to protect the corporation's interests in exchange for cold hard cash. With 5 different theaters of operations (of varying difficulty) and an interesting mix of aerial-style submarine tactics, you'll be fighting fierce battles for corporate territory beneath the waves.

429607.overview: Fasten your seat belts, bring your seat back to an upright position, you are about to pilot a Federation Starship on a wild roller coaster ride through the final frontier.

429744.overview: The Forgotten Realm Archives - Collection Two brings a healthy mix of “Gold Box” and nostalgia goodness to your PC, along with a combination of adventure builders, turn-based and real-time role-playing gameplay. Composed of RPG classics that premiered the Forgotten Realms to video gamers, The Forgotten Realm Archives - Collection Two contains the following titles: Pool of Radiance, Curse of the Azure Bonds, Hillsfar, Secret of the Silver Blades, Pools of Darkness, Gateway to the Savage Frontier, Treasures of the Savage Frontier, Forgotten Realms Unlimited Adventures.

441753.overview: The Empire stretches its evil clutches across the galaxy, consuming planets with devastating results. Through many struggles, the Rebel Alliance has learned of a new Imperial battle station, the Death Star, with enough power to destroy an entire planet.

442199.overview:
In Sexy Fighter, the story unfolds as students inadvertently unleash the devil, leading to the unexpected takeover of the entire school. Our protagonist, Meiya, embarks on a mission to vanquish the queen of Hades and restore order to the school. Along the journey, players engage in battles and undergo upgrades reminiscent of traditional role-playing games. 

The combat mechanics introduce a unique twist, employing a card-based system for both offense and defense, deviating from the conventional fighting game format. Each player wields a set of five cards, strategically choosing their actions to outsmart their opponent and emerge victorious. Sexy Fighter offers a fresh and dynamic gameplay experience, blending elements of card games with the immersive world-building of RPGs.

447472.overview: SimCity: Terrain Editor enables the player to edit their city's environment by placing rivers, lakes, islands, trees, etc. It also allows to clean instantaneously all man-made features of an existing city. Nine to eighteen ready to use cities are also included.

447527.overview: This add-on for the original release of SimCity adds three different alternate looks to the game: Ancient Asia, Medieval Times and Wild West. Gameplay is unchanged by installation of the Graphics Set, but all in-game graphics and text are replaced. Buildings all look different, and the various events and disasters are reinterpreted and given a different flavor.

447533.overview: This add-on for the original release of SimCity adds three different alternate looks to the game: Future U.S.A., Future Europe and Moon Colony. Gameplay is unchanged by installation of the Graphics Set, but all in-game graphics and text are replaced. Buildings all look different, and the various events and disasters are reinterpreted and given a different flavor.

449627.overview:
In this type-in BASIC game from Compute! magazine, the player takes control of a ship beset by an unfortunate set of circumstances. Not only is it trapped in a series of caverns (presumably in space), it's also given a less-than-welcoming reception by the local residents - a rather unfriendly bunch of aliens. In each room, four of them will try to chase down your ship, and you'll only have your forward-firing gun to get you by.

Once the room is cleared of aliens, it's on to the next one; the rooms are grouped into levels, each with more rooms than the last. Between levels, you will be treated to a bonus round, which lets you take revenge on your pursuers: the aliens are now stationary, and you will have to hunt down as many as you can before time runs out. In each session, the game keeps track of the three highest scores.

454764.overview:
Sink the Fleet is a computerized version of the board game Battleship. Players compete to locate and sink their opponent’s fleet on a grid-based battlefield. The game can be played in single-player mode against the computer or with two human players.

Before gameplay begins, players place their ships on the grid and take turns firing at coordinates to hit and sink the opponent’s fleet. The game includes multiple difficulty levels for computer opponents and allows progress to be saved and resumed later.

454775.overview: Super Pac-Man is an adaptation of the classic Pac-Man with the added benefit of being playable by two players at the same time. It features 20 levels and an editor for easy level creation. Requires Sound Blaster 2.0 for Sound Blaster audio (not compatible with SB16). Music and effects by Juan Miguel López.

455358.overview:
The Secret Codes of C.Y.P.H.E.R.: Operation U.S. Presidents is an educational game and the sequel to The Secret Codes of C.Y.P.H.E.R.: Operation Wildlife. It teaches children about U.S. Presidents and about logic and language skills by utilizing 5 decoder alphabets: English, American Sign Language, Braille, Morse Code, and Semaphore.

You play as a C.Y.P.H.E.R. (Courageous Young Partners in Hush-Hush Electronic Radiotelegraphy) who must locate and decode CYPHERGRAMS and then deliver them to your client. Agents must beware of L.U.R.K.'s (Loathsome Underhanded Rotten Krooks) who will try to steal the CYPHERGRAMS.

Players will be able to access the built in FunCyclopedia, which contains over 1,000 facts about the life and times of U.S. Presidents. In addition, basic cryptography is taught with the 5 decoder alphabets.

Players can select from four levels of difficulty.

455359.overview:
This is an adventure game in a similar vein to Where in the World is Carmen SanDiego, although the questions deal with additional topics besides geography (science, weather, history, etc.). And instead of pursuing a variety of henchmen leading-up to Carmen SanDiego, each puzzle is just another step towards stopping Dr. Data.

The game is based on a book of the same name.

455452.overview:
A Megaman-style platformer, it's based on the Manga series Skull Man (Sukaru Man) by Shotaro Ishinomori.
Originally an MS-DOS game by Diogo Lapa, it was reprogrammed to work with BennuGD by GECAsoft.

455666.overview:
The Sierra Network later rebranded as the ImagiNation Network, was an online service launched in 1991 by Sierra On-Line. It offered subscribers a unique online space to play games and socialize, billing itself as a "cyberspace theme park." This service was the first exclusively focused on online gaming and was among the early adopters of online avatars, laying the groundwork for future gaming communities.

The Town Hall: Offered administrative services, including billing details and an events calendar.

The Mall: The Mall initially offered physical copies of Sierra games and branded T-shirts via mail-order. The aim was to eventually evolve into a digital distribution platform for Sierra games.

The Post Office: Allowed members to send and receive email.

The Clubhouse: Provided access to traditional games such as chess, checkers, bridge, and backgammon.

SierraLand: All-ages experiences with games like miniature golf, paintball, the Red Baron flight simulator, and Graffiti, a program for drawing and creativity.

LarryLand: Catered to adults with a theme park inspired by the Leisure Suit Larry series, offering casino games and a virtual bar for socializing. The platform encourages playful interactions like electronic kisses, under the watchful eye of system operators to maintain appropriate conduct.

The Shadow of Yserbius: A role-playing game set in Mount Yserbius' dungeons, filled with monsters and puzzles. It combined traditional RPG elements like turn-based combat and character development, paving the way for future online games with its mix of gameplay and social interaction.

455956.overview: Sexy Puzzle/Strip Puzzle is one of those puzzles that became fashionable in the eighties, where a drawing is divided into small squares that you have to move, with the aim that they all fit together perfectly, as an example, the first phase of Journey to the Center of the Earth.

456150.overview: This expansion for Redneck Rampage comprises 75 levels and 15 multiplayer levels and maps, which were chosen from a contest conducted for the game.

456152.overview: Released in 1992 on DOS, It's an action game, set in an arcade theme. Classic snake game in Norwegian. Collect the items, grow longer, and survive for as long (time and size!) as possible.

456158.overview: Space Guardian is a clone of the old Star Trek text strategy game. As commander of the GUARDIAN, the player must find all ships of the Alien empire by locating them using the scanner, firing torpedoes while defending against enemy attacks by raising the shields.

456224.overview:
Star Trek: Strategic Operations Simulator (also known as Star Trek: SOS and Star Trek Arcade) is a space combat simulation arcade game based on the original Star Trek television program and movie series, and released by Sega in 1983.

Unlike most arcade games of the time, the player is presented with multiple views of the play field. Throughout the game, survival depends on the player's ability to effectively use and manage shield energy, photon torpedoes, and warp energy. These are replenished by docking with starbases, which sometimes must be saved from destruction at the hands of the Klingons.

456579.overview:
An unofficial PC port of the 1984 game released only for MSX and ColecoVision. In terms of genre, it is a vertical flying game with non-stop (that's right!) action.

There is a plot: the future, an army of evil Zefurian aliens invaded Earth in their powerful flying machines. Humanity can be saved from destruction by a pilot who controls a unique experimental machine - the Sky Jaguar. The ultimate goal of the game is to destroy the main headquarters of the enemy, but for this you will have to defeat many enemies...

Probably, formally we can say that this game does not differ in variety. The levels are very similar to each other, the enemies are of the same type (just airplanes, in fact), there is no variety of weapons either. But Sky Jaguar is valuable for something completely different - complexity. A real "old" difficulty, sometimes simply deadly: there are often situations when missiles fired by enemies fill half of the screen, so it will be very difficult to dodge them. And most importantly, you can't relax here even for a second, because the action, as already mentioned, does not stop. Under no circumstances should you use this game for "fun" - it does not forgive it.

It is also worth noting that graphically Sky Jaguar is one of the most beautiful games released on MSX (and the MSX version was ported to PC), so the landscapes and even the enemies themselves from a visual point of view can pleasantly surprise connoisseurs of old beauties. Due to the long-standing appearance of this unofficial port, this item can already be considered a PC game (like a number of other games ported from MSX in this way), so all fans of truly complex flying games should definitely take a look at it.

456977.overview: The Third Reich is storming across Mother Russia. This game recreates multiple battles between the Germans and Soviets in 1941 till 1943 in 9 total scenarios. The battlefield is structured as a 36 by 18/36 hexagonal grid. Each scenario must be completed within a limited number of turns, effectively utilizing a set number of combat units.

458239.overview:
A very curious - albeit primitive - Spanish fighting game, all the fighters in which are anthropomorphic hot dogs, and presented with the maximum possible "originality": among them there are "Chinese", "black", "woman", "robot" and so on. The plot as such seems to be absent.

Before the start, you can choose any character you like, after which the computer will automatically determine the opponent. The player is required to defeat the opponent in two rounds out of three, - in this case, there is a return to the menu with protagonists, where you will need to mark someone new as your alter ego - they will no longer be allowed to control the newly won one in the current "tournament" again. In case of loss, the action simply ends, and a restart is required to continue.

The gameplay is quite simple: all characters, formally (formally) differing in health, can jump, crouch and inflict two types of blows: with the upper and lower limbs (the Alt and Space keys are responsible for the latter, respectively); The second type of blows mentioned is much more powerful, and with the help of this tactic, diluted with occasional jumps, it will certainly not be difficult to defeat anyone with anyone.

From the point of view of graphics, everything looks quite cute (although very "simple" for the year of release), moderately funny; A variety of backgrounds are used as "arenas" - from the desert to a room in a mansion; Moreover, in fact, each such location is larger than the game screen - it is scrolled ("side-scrolling"), and the fighters can move to the left and right, thereby opening up new views. Despite the mentioned simplicity of the picture, there are many animation effects, mainly related to the facial expressions of the characters, which change according to the situation during the battle.

It is difficult to say anything else: unusual in theme, fantastically rare (and of completely unclear origin), but a very simple and, let's be honest, not particularly exciting thing. So the recommendations are primarily for collectors and children (fortunately, there is no visual violence here).

458270.overview: A game created by a single person (Carlos Esteve Cremades) and marketed at newsstands by Magim Ediciones (formerly Ediciones Manali, later Ediciones Mago).

458309.overview:
"Starcop is a fixed-screen, retro sci-fi arcade shoot-'em-up developed and published by Ediciones Manali. In a premise heavily inspired by classic 80s space patrol tropes, players step into the cockpit of a specialized, cross-shaped interstellar interceptor ship. As an elite member of the galactic police defense force, your assignment is to patrol deep-space sectors and protect the system from waves of invading space pirate fleets.

The gameplay loop centers entirely on fixed-screen tactical action. Players slide their starship horizontally across the bottom margin of the display screen, actively aiming firing vectors upward to clear out grid formations of incoming raider craft. Beyond standard ship navigation, users must precisely track a dual metric interface mapping their active shields and localized defensive battery cells.

True to the architectural limits of early 1990s Spanish budget computing compilations, the engine operates entirely within a strict 4-color CGA graphics configuration (cyan, magenta, black, and white). The title features a striking, stylized split-art loading matrix showcasing a digitized profile of an armored space marshal wearing reflective visors."

458315.overview:
Let's go over a little history. A few years ago, the feudal lord of our county appointed me as the lifelong defender of our village. How could I have imagined this would happen? The only thing we know about the strange beings is that they're on the outskirts, and from the mouth of an old man (an old man) who wasn't very lucid himself.

It turns out that the aforementioned aliens are running out of energy, and the only thing that could replace them was STARLIFE, which was also on the best planet in the universe. I don't say "best" because of its virtues, but because its inhabitants were "prim" enough to be able to take it without any problem.

Hehe!! What they don't know is that our alter ego will defend us. Because that's the case, right? The answer is in your hands, although personally I don't think you'll succeed; you're not good enough for such an endeavor. Or maybe you are?

458499.overview: The Count of Monte Cristo was eventually consumed entirely by his drive for revenge. Count Cristo, on the other hand, is merely the victim of a Voodoo curse an enemy hexed him with... an external plague more possible to reverse. Starting the game standing over his coffin, you wander the length and breadth of his castle in pursuit of a recipe and the verbal and material components needed to cast an antidote to counter his occult menace. It contains good-luck charms, the sorts of mad scientist chemical concoctions that might well yield a Jekyll-and-Hyde transformation, a flighty medium and her crystal ball, and no small quantity of juju, useful for all sorts of voodoo applications. All that and a chimneysweep trapped in the flue! The player will navigate all these and more with the trademark Adventure International VERB NOUN two-word text parser.

458958.overview:
Everyone in the insane asylum knew that Bowls was not as crazy as he looked. Years ago, his heroism

He had saved the nation from a nuclear disaster. However, because of that frantic

adventure, his mental health had been somewhat deteriorated.

One morning, two guys dressed in Special Forces suits came to the clinic carrying

an order to take Bowls with him. The disaster had occurred again, but this time its

mission would not have the Earth as destiny ...

458971.overview: On board your interplanetary ship, you must move zarte to each of the invaded planets and neutralize mutant enemies. The end is with the deadliest of these beings: the Spiders-Alien, whose shell makes them immune to all kinds of shots. The only way to eliminate them is make them fall through the grids on the floor, lifting them when they approach you and then close to catch their fingers. In addition, you must collect the biological specimens from each planet represented by small hearts. Once you have eliminated all the Spiders-Alien and collected all the specimens you can escape from planet.

459169.overview: In Sabotaje you are a forklift looking for switches and keys to move through a warehouse filled with enemies, lasers, and traps. Your fuel level is constantly dropping, so you must keep moving and look for canisters to replenish your stock.The ultimate goal is to use the forklift to locate a missle and bring it back to the first screen of the game.

459482.overview:
The game itself is not a "revelation": it is an ordinary arcade shooter with a side view in which we need to control the funny kind of machine with a cannon (similar to a buggy), destroying over five fairly extensive levels of various enemies (and on one from them the machine has to swim).

Graphically Supercyberlooks very good: 256-color VGA-palette, the gamma is bright, the drawing is clear, there are special effects. Playing in Spanish, but understanding the meaning of the phrases in the menu is quite simple, there is no other text in it; management is also "Spanish" (and here with it there can be certain difficulties, if before you did not play the Spanish arcades). In general - a good game, which for today, of course, is more interested in its rarity and mysterious origin.

460160.overview:
S80-Mechanik is a Mechanik EN57 modification that recreates the German S-Bahn S80 line, featuring the ÖBB Class 4020 EMU. The mod allows players to explore an authentic German suburban route, bringing a new cultural and operational setting to the simulator.

Because the project remains incomplete, the cab of the Polish EN57 has been used as a functional substitute. While not an exact representation of the Class 4020’s driving environment, it ensures the route is fully playable and enjoyable until a dedicated 4020 cab can be developed.

Despite this limitation, S80-Mechanik stands out for its faithful recreation of the S80 line and represents a significant expansion of Mechanik into German-speaking railway territory.

460549.overview: Explore the unbelievable world of science with Science Adventure II from Knowledge Adventure. For the first time ever on your personal computer, experience virtual reality.

461139.overview:
Super Baseball 2020 is a futuristic baseball video game only released in South Korea for both MS-DOS and Windows.

The game follows the basic rules of baseball, but there are several upgrades since the game takes place in the year 2020. The most obvious difference from real baseball is that some of the characters in this game are robots. All the human characters are equipped with powerful armor, computer sensors, and jet-packs for improved offense and defensive skills.

464290.overview: Strike reproduces a full game of ten-pin bowling for one or two players. Before each roll, the player positions the bowler along the approach and times the throw to set the ball’s power and direction. The ball then travels down the isometric lane toward the pins, with the outcome shown on an overhead pin display. Scoring follows standard bowling rules, including strikes, spares, and bonus throws in the tenth frame. Games can be played against a friend or a computer-controlled opponent.

464568.overview:
The Solar Hockey League is a Shareware Sports game published by Galifir Developments in 1992.

A better name for this game might be "advanced air hockey". The game plays kind of like air hockey (with 3 paddles per side) and kind of like regular hockey / table hockey. The object is to score on your opponent's goal. The game's graphics and sound are minimal, but you can play both a two player game and a game against a tough computer opponent. Tiny file size too!

465654.overview: The player helps navigate Ernie's rubber duck to his bathtub. To do this, the player must place a number of blocks on the screen which redirect the duck's movement so that it reaches the square with the bathtub. The total play area is 5 x 5 squares. The player can use as many tiles as they wish to make this happen. Pieces are placed based upon the duck's movement, and then the duck's trip is animated.

465844.overview:
Strategic Craps is a betting simulator and craps game.

Designed to teach players the game of craps, and help them improve their technique. Numerous betting strategies and tutorials are embedded within the game, and the player can also play individual games of craps to test their technique. The craps board is graphically displayed on the screen during gameplay.

The player can also create a craps strategy, where they bet specific ways for different rolls and situations. The player can then simulate a number of rounds to see how their strategy performs, and their expected gambling returns.

465848.overview:
Scrabble is a licensed version of the popular Spear's game developed by U.S. Gold

Scrabble is a word game for 2 - 4 players. It is played by forming interlocking words, cross-word style, on a Scrabble playing board. The Scrabble board is a grid on which there are bonus squares, playing a letter on one of these squares doubles or triples the score for either the letter or the entire word. Players have seven letters, or tiles, each and at the end of each turn, they take new letters from a pile, unseen, to replace the letters used.

465849.overview: Sea War: Entscheidungsschlacht im Pazifik is based on the classic turn-based board game Battleship. Play against the AI or another player. Place your fleet on a 12x12 tiles board and try to hit the enemy's ships by selecting a field. You play for as long as you sink the ship or miss. If you sink the whole fleet, you win. Different ships from two tiles up to 5 tiles are available.

465851.overview: This is a word processor program that teaches children to write and print words, sentences and stories, with help from Big Bird, Cookie Monster, Oscar the Grouch and Elmo.

465855.overview: Spell-A-Saurus is an educational game for elementary school children. The game has a prehistoric theme using dinosaur characters. It consists of four mini-games: AstroDrive, Zug Escape, Ptera-Ptutor, and Spell-A-Saur, centered around unscrambling, spelling, or otherwise writing words. The player can choose a list of words to use for each game, or create one from scratch. Spell-A-Saurus also has an early text-to-speech feature with compatible sound drivers.

465856.overview: Race from coast to coast across the southern USA in this stock car racer, which takes you from Florida to California through freeways, bridges, side routes and country roads (and if you're so inclined, through houses and water bodies too). As your car zooms in top-down view along the bends, forks and intersections, your only rival is the clock - represented by a fuel tank that only lasts 90 seconds, no matter your speed.

465862.overview: An arcade game with some puzzle elements that is said to take place in 2025, where 'Skate Dragon' is a popular and very dangerous TV show. A person on skates is to cross levels of platforms, each of them occupying one single screen, and to reach the exit door, while struggling with and avoiding different menaces and obstacles that include ice coating, dragons breathing fire or shooting small balls etc.

465863.overview:
Spellicopter is an educational software game that enables children to develop their spelling skills in order to remain in flight. The screen display shows speed, altitude, fuel level, score and cargo. It offers three levels of difficulty, allowing the student to learn up to 400 words, in 40 categories, in beginner, intermediate and advanced modes.

The program could be played using keyboard or joystick, giving a sentence context clue for each word, allowing the student to maintain altitude and speed for correct spellings, utilizing screen graphics, animation and sound effects.

466557.overview: Survival is a post-apocalyptic strategy game that takes place after a nuclear war on devastated earth. Together with a small group of survivors the player has to leave the bunker and try to built up a new future. Mutants and other survivors will challenge this ambitions while building up a new civilization.

468920.overview: Shadow of the Lost Citadel is a clunky third-person fantasy game that was released in 2001. It plays like a tech demo and was far too late in the day for its release. The game is available for download on platforms like RomStation, where players can manage their games directly from the application. However, it has been noted that the game is quite boring and monotonous, with some players finding it not really fun to play.

468997.overview: The Search for Freedom is a role-playing game that combines fantasy and tactical RPG elements. It was published in 1996 and is available for DOS. The game features a first-person perspective, allowing players to explore a town and catacombs, interact with NPCs, and engage in character creation and party systems. It also includes a long storyline that informs the player's adventures.

469725.overview:
A medieval fantasy beat-'em-up set in the ancient Korean kingdom of Baekje, The Soul incorporates some RPG elements along with a non-linear structure. One or two players can choose from five playable characters: Won Sul Rang, Jeong Do Ryung, Hiromi, Heuk Chi Sang Chi and Seok Hye Tong - a group of battle-mages who had fallen afoul of a powerful weretiger/sorcerer. The latter's machinations are upsetting the balance of good and evil in the kingdom. After encountering a group of seemingly possessed Tang soldiers, who turn hostile, the party sets out to restore cosmic harmony.

The characters all have their own unique strengths, weaknesses, special moves and magic attacks, with which to carve their way through the armies of soldiers, sorcerers and fantastical creatures that await them. These skills can be strengthened at the end of each stage - the 'level up points' you have gained can be distributed amongst your character stats: health, strength, intelligence and five different magical skills.

On many occasions, after a stage has been completed, you will have a multiple choice of destinations; you can set your own path through the realm, and the sequence of stages can vary from game to game. You're only given a single life (once you're out of health, it's game over), but four save slots are provided to compensate for the difficulty.

469965.overview:
It is a Spanish game that supports CGA and VGA, similar to the one on the Super Scrylis website by Topo Soft, but by Goldy Games and released on the disc attached to the 9th issue of the Spanish magazine PC Mania.

The game is clearly inspired by the Rubik's Cube and similar puzzles. We have two rings with faces made of squares of different colors, and by shifting the edges of the lower body, it needs to be "remade" in the same way as the upper one - and time passes, lowering bonus points and threatening to take away "lives" to the measured biper ticking.

Control - rotate the entire "assembly" around the center "one step" with the cursors left and right, up and down - turn the segment of the lower body facing the player "across the bagel"; Shift rotates the "ring" of these faces to the left and right, respectively, Alt and Ctrl rotate the upper body. The Q, A, O, P keys simply rotate the player's point of view "in three dimensions" (and in CGA mode, X switches the palette). Like any "rubicoid", it is addictive, but, fortunately, at the start you can choose a level from the first to the "current".

In general, it is a great pastime for lovers of casual puzzles: "outwardly simple, but tasteful".

470409.overview:
The plot is simple. After sizzling global nuclear conflict with the human genome everything finally went somehow "wrong". People have become mutants, resulting in a long time they have to be in the biological condition of the dragons. While these dragons in the game are mostly the most that neither is a common dinosaurs (reptilian theory supporters rejoice!). In general, outside of the ring all of these fighters for ecological reasons unknown to us are forced to eke out their miserable existence in the form of mindless dinosaurs, and only in brief moments of uncompromising struggle, they regain the ability to be a short time people.

Fighters only eight, and they are all colorful, because, as has been said, people "a little bit" mutated. The first fighter named Attila, politically correct to put it - a hybrid of human and bird dog. Next comes Chios - man-cat, is nothing unusual: only the claws on his hands and a mustache on his face. There is still Pliny - very muscular fighter. Pliny escaped severe mutations, but his hair is steel blue. Then comes Rauric - a soldier dressed in armor. With Rauric in terms of genetics is also all right, but one of the brushes (left) in his amputated and replaced it attached to a hand prosthesis - a sharp sword. Of course, in any fighting game must be present, and women fighters. 471172.overview: Subterraneans was originally developed as a 3D shooter using the DOS-based “Pie in the Sky” engine, structured with a level design inspired by the classic Wolfenstein architecture. The game was intended to be released in 1996 by Full Moon, but it remained an unfinished project, making it one of the more obscure DOS titles from the era. Specific details about the storyline are limited since the project did not reach full commercial completion.

472286.overview:
SPWW2 (which stands for Steel Panthers World War II) is an authorised stand-alone expansion for SSI's Steel Panthers II. It contains several hundred scenarios set mainly in the timeframe of the Second World War but also covering some battles of the interbellum period, as well as a number campaigns, either based on historical events or exploring alternate history scenarios.

Built on a vastly modified source code of the original Steel Panthers II, the game features numerous enhancements, including an expanded set of units and terrain types, increased limits for various in-game objects, improved AI and random scenario/campaign generator, and cheat countermeasures for play-by-email (PBEM) games. Additionally, SPWW2 includes a scenario editor, campaign editor and unit editor allowing for maximum customisation of the game by the players.

474614.overview: The third instalment of the Scythe series. Released episodically, with Episodes 1-2 (10 maps).

474989.overview: Special Corps is an obscure 1995 Spanish/Argentine shooting‑gallery game with four nearly identical missions, crude digitized backgrounds, and simple enemy sprites. The player shoots stationary training targets before each mission and then fights repetitive enemies who barely move and rarely pose real danger. The game offers no interface, no visible score, seemingly infinite health, and missions end abruptly even if enemies remain alive. Only the third mission stands out—a hostage scenario where you must repeatedly shoot a bandit without hitting the girl he’s holding. Graphics are inconsistent, perspective is off, and the overall experience is dull. The reviewer concludes it’s only of interest to collectors of rare curiosities, not actual players.

475249.overview:
Super Nibbly is a Snake-variant where you control a worm in a maze, eating pills while growing. The game is a successor to the previous game by the same developer, Nibbly '92. The game starts with an overview map, where the snake moves on a path on a group of islands, going from location to location while having some non-interactive funny animation events on the way. At each named village, the game switches to a maze screen where the player can control the snake. The mazes are similar in layout as the Pac-Man style maze, a fixed single screen, only without enemies.

The objective is for the snake to eat all pills/cookies in the maze, before returning to the overhead map and moving to the next location.

The player controls the snake's movement one step at a time, and there is some strategy involved in navigating the mazes, while there also is a timer ticking down.

The rules are that the snake can move forward, or to the side, and avoid being blocked by its own body from moving anywhere.

Eating a pill makes the snake grow one segment longer. There are special objects appearing in the maze for a limited time, that can affect how the snake grows (longer/shorter), or give extra points, a time extension or a special object called a 'puck'. In some locations there are dead-ends, which if entered could trap the snake, but it can shoot a puck (which looks as if it split off its head) into these locations, and so get all pills in the dead-end.

Each location has multiple mazes to traverse before the player returns to the overhead map.

Failing to avoid the snake's own body loses a life, and the maze restarts anew. Fail three times and it's game over.

480054.overview: Sergeant Slotte: Galaxy Janitor is a vertical-scrolling space shoot 'em up developed by CSW Group and published by Mad Data for MS-DOS in 1995. Built around a satirical, environmental premise, the game details a crisis where humanity's deep-space garbage disposal methods accidentally pollute a sovereign alien planet. Seeking retaliation, the extraterrestrials send a colossal mothership to dump the terrestrial trash back into Earth's orbit. Players pilot a defensive janitorial starcraft to vaporize structural hazards and salvage floating cosmic debris.The gameplay relies on vertical arcade scrolling dynamics, tasking players with steering a green-and-blue multi-winged fighter craft along the bottom margin of a starfield grid. Instead of navigating traditional military dogfights, the pilot must blast floating space junk—ranging from discarded computer monitors and CRT chassis to biochemical flasks, bones, and batteries—while dodging defensive energy fields. Operating on a vibrant 256-color VGA palette with an integrated cockpit hud tracking shield capacities and weapon temperature gauges, the title stands as an incredibly rare and distinct example of late-era DOS shareware humor.

480094.overview:
Star Wars: Making Magic is an interactive CD-ROM released in 1996 by LucasArts as part of The LucasArts Archives Vol. II: Star Wars Collection and its Mac edition. It was also included on the CD for Star Wars: Yoda Stories, released in 1997. It was designed as a behind-the-scenes look at the production of Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition release.

It includes interviews with George Lucas revealing why he chose to re-touch and add to the original trilogy. It also includes documentaries on the process behind enhancing existing scenes and adding new computer generated imagery into the original films.

While not containing as extensive a collection of previously deleted scenes or cut-content as Behind the Magic, Making Magic does include some of the original scene of Han Solo and Jabba the Hutt meeting in Docking Bay 94. The scene (as originally filmed in 1976 with Harrison Ford and Irish actor Declan Mulholland, prior to a CGI Jabba being added) was briefly seen in the television specials The Making of Star Wars in 1977 and From Star Wars to Jedi: The Making of a Saga in 1983.

482535.overview: Léto s Oskarem (internationally known as Summer with Oscar) is a classic 2D cartoon point-and-click adventure game released for MS-DOS in 1998. Developed by a small team led by Pavel Širůček, it holds a significant place in Czech gaming history as the final adventure game published by Vochozka Trading right before the company transformed into the legendary studio Illusion Softworks (creators of the original Mafia and Hidden & Dangerous).

482709.overview: The shipwrecked Gajbraš Trípvůd searches a strange island for a way home. Talk to eccentric inhabitants, collect items and solve puzzles in cartoon locations. This Czech comedy adventure parodies the pirate world of Monkey Island through wordplay and absurd situations.

482710.overview: A shepherd sets out to break the wizard Swigrid's curse before eternal snow and ice bury his home and friends. Explore a fairy-tale world, talk to its inhabitants and use collected objects to solve puzzles. The adventure features Czech voice acting.

482732.overview: An unofficial DOS platformer recreates the style and assets of Super Mario World. Its five levels include familiar enemies, power-up mushrooms and fire flowers, with jumping and exploration at the centre of play.
